name: Beef tendons
h1: Beef tendons for dogs made in USA: what each brand's page says
title: Beef tendons made in USA: what 6 brand pages say | Nibbables
meta: Which beef tendons say made in USA? 3 of 6 brand pages we list name the USA (Pupford; Sancho & Lola's Closet); none say both made and sourced there. Exact quotes on each card.
intro: Looking for beef tendons for dogs made in the USA? Of the 6 beef tendon product pages we list, 3 name the USA in their made-in or sourcing wording: Pupford Thick Beef Tendon Dog Chew (“Made in the USA”), Sancho & Lola's Closet USA Beef Tendons (“gourmet dog chews made from American-sourced beef”), and Sancho & Lola's Closet USA Flexor Tendons - DELISH! (“Made in Colorado.”). None of those 3 say both made and sourced in the USA on the same page — Pupford also says “These chews are sourced in Colombia.” The other 3 name Paraguay or don't state a country. Each card below quotes the brand's exact wording; Nibbables doesn't rank brands.

name: Fish skin chews
h1: Fish skin dog chews: what cod, wolffish and salmon skin brands say
title: Fish skin dog chews by brand: origin, fat & calories | Nibbables
meta: Cod, wolffish and salmon skin dog chews from 4 brands, with ingredients, origin, fat and calorie figures and size guidance quoted from each brand's own page.
intro: Fish skin chews are dried cod, wolffish or salmon skins, sold rolled, wrapped into sticks or as whole skins. If you're asking whether fish skins are good for dogs, the brand pages below make nutrition claims (omega-3s, protein, dental support) in their own words, and we leave those claims on their pages rather than repeat them as fact. What we compare is what each page states: the one ingredient, where the fish is from and where the chew is made, the fat and calorie figures, and which dog sizes it names. The fat figures differ a lot: the cod and wolffish skins here list 1% to 4.49% fat, while Jack's Premium lists 18% for its smoked salmon skins. Anything a page doesn't say is marked Not stated. Ask your vet whether a fish skin chew suits your dog.

name: Pig ears

title: Pig ear dog chews by brand: origin, fat & calories | Nibbables
meta: Pig ear dog chews from 4 brands, with ingredients, where they're made and sourced, fat and calorie figures and size wording quoted from each brand's page.
intro: Pig ears are dried, sometimes smoked, pork ears sold whole, halved or sliced. If you're asking whether pig ears are good for dogs, the brand pages below make their own claims, and we leave those on their pages rather than repeat them as fact. What we compare is what each page states: the ingredient, where the pork comes from and where the chew is made, the fat and calorie figures, and which dogs it names. The stated origins differ: one page says sourced and made in the USA, one says pork from Brazil, and Redbarn lists Canada, Mexico and South Korea for its natural ears. The stated minimum fat runs from 5% to 9% on the pages that list it. Anything a page doesn't say is marked Not stated. Ask your vet whether a pig ear suits your dog.

name: Cow hooves

title: Cow hoof dog chews by brand: origin, fillings & calories
meta: Cow hoof dog chews from 4 brands, plain and filled, with ingredients, where they're made and sourced, and size and supervision wording quoted from each page.
intro: Cow hooves are cleaned, dried or baked beef hooves, sold plain or with a filling in the hollow center. If you're asking whether cow hooves are good for dogs, we leave each brand's claims on its own page and compare only what the pages state: the ingredients, where the hooves come from and where they're made, the fat and calorie figures, and which chewers each brand names. Plain and filled hooves differ a lot: the plain hooves list one ingredient, while the filled ones list a filling with corn syrup, sugar and preservatives. Stated origins include Brazil, Australia and the USA. Pawstruck's page warns that natural hooves may splinter or break. Anything a page doesn't say is marked Not stated. Ask your vet whether a hoof suits your dog.

intro: Cow ears are dried or oven-baked beef ears, sold whole, plain or washed ("white"), and thick-cut. If you're asking whether cow ears are good for dogs, or how they compare with pig ears, we compare only what each brand's own page states: the ingredients, where the ears come from or are made, calorie and guaranteed-analysis figures, and the chewer sizes and supervision steps each brand names. Stated origins differ a lot between brands: Brazil, Colombia, Canada, the USA and Turkey all appear. Only one page gives calories per ear. Anything a page doesn't say is marked Not stated. Ask your vet whether a cow ear suits your dog.

name: Lamb and goat horns
h1: Lamb and goat horn dog chews: what each brand says about origin, size and fat
title: Lamb & goat horn dog chews by brand: origin, size & fat
meta: Lamb and goat horn dog chews from 3 brands, with ingredients, origin, size guidance, fat figures and supervision notes quoted from each brand page.
intro: Lamb and goat horns are single-ingredient keratin chews sold as a long-lasting option for dogs that chew hard. Brands describe them as made of keratin (not bone), sometimes with marrow inside. If you're looking up a lamb horn dog chew or a goat horn for dogs, we compare only what each brand's own page states: the ingredient, where the horn comes from, size and weight ranges, fat and calorie figures where listed, and the supervision steps each brand names. Stated origins differ (Turkey; free-range Icelandic lamb; Jack's Premium does not name a country on its goat horn page). Ask your vet whether a hard horn chew suits your dog's teeth and chewing style.
